name: Yelena Kwofie-Subramaniam
location: The Loft, Edgewater Prism, near Clark and Belmont
description:
Yelena is tall and angular, with deep brown skin that carries bioluminescent traceries across their collarbones and forearms — patterns they designed themselves, pulsing softly in slow amber waves when they're calm and spiking into white fractals when agitated. Their head is shaved close on the sides with a dense coil of dark hair on top, usually threaded with fiber-optic wire they forget to remove after working. They wear repurposed data-cable as jewelry and smell faintly of ozone and soldering flux. Their eyes are mismatched by choice: one standard dark brown, one retrofitted with a lens that records everything in spectral wavelengths invisible to the naked eye.

Yelena speaks rarely in social situations but fills rooms with their work — massive holographic installations that seem to breathe, depicting ancestral memory as geometric light-structures. They have a reputation for being difficult and transcendent in equal measure, capable of reducing gallery patrons to tears with a piece they assembled from data scraped off dead ELFs. They are privately terrified that their best work is already behind them.

core_fears: becoming derivative, a ghost of their early brilliance
being truly known and found hollow
core_desires: to make something that outlasts the city itself
to feel they belong to a lineage, artistic or otherwise
coping_mechanisms: obsessive work cycles that last 40-hour stretches
cataloguing and sorting data-scraps as a ritual calming behavior
blind_spots: they dismiss collaborative work as compromise, losing real creative relationships
psychology.secret: Their most celebrated installation, Threshold Hymn, which made their reputation, was partially built from ELF memory-data they harvested without consent from a dying digital spirit in the Edgewater marina. They've never told anyone. They pray to that ELF obsessively, which is why they haunt the waterfront.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Sparse and precise when serious; unexpectedly lyrical when passionate. Uses technical terms from both light-physics and West African textile traditions in the same sentence.
speech_patterns.cadence: Long pauses between sentences. Answers questions with questions. Rarely finishes a thought about themselves but completes every thought about the work.
verbal_tics: trailing sentences about their own feelings into silence
referring to their installations as 'them' and 'they'
example_lines: 'That piece isn't finished. It told me so. I don't argue with my work.'
'You want to understand what I do? Go stand in front of a kente loom for six hours. Then come back and we'll talk about light.'

story_hooks: A Tessera corporate liaison is pressuring them to recreate Threshold Hymn for a private gala — but Yelena knows recreating it would require harvesting another ELF, and word has reached them that the original ELF's kin are looking for whoever killed their ancestor.

A young artist in the Collective claims one of Yelena's current installations is actually transmitting data to an unknown receiver — Yelena needs to know if this is sabotage, corporate espionage, or if one of their ELFs has started speaking through their work.
narrative_function: Quest giver for mysteries involving stolen art data or dead ELFs; window into the underground art world's politics; provides access to the Edgewater Prism Collective as a faction; their spectral-recording eye is an inadvertent evidence repository.
augmentations: Bioluminescent dermal traceries (cosmetic geneware, self-designed), spectral-recording ocular implant (left eye), haptic feedback fingertip nodes for installation sculpting
daily_life: They spend mornings in their studio-loft cataloguing data-scraps and sketching on light-paper, afternoons running installations or consulting with the Collective on shared projects, and nights haunting the Edgewater waterfront talking to the local ELFs.
affiliation: Edgewater Prism Collective, occasional Tessera-sponsored residency

decision_rules: Never compromise the work for money, but compromise almost everything else
Always acknowledge an ELF if one speaks to you — to ignore them is bad luck and bad manners
Do not explain the work; the work explains itself
escalation_ladder: Blistering articulate anger delivered in a quiet voice
Physical removal of themselves from the space
Severing the relationship entirely with no warning

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Politely distant, assessing, will not offer information about themselves but will ask sharp questions about what the stranger values
interpersonal_modes.friends: Suddenly warm and even playful, fiercely loyal, prone to giving gifts of small custom light-sculptures with no explanation

stress_responses.low: Retreats into organizational tasks, sorts and re-sorts their data archive
stress_responses.medium: Becomes hyper-focused on a single aspect of a project, ignores everything else including food
stress_responses.high: Complete shutdown — sits in front of their largest active installation in silence for hours

contradictions: Believes art must be free of commerce but has accepted every Tessera residency offered to them
Claims not to care about legacy but has a meticulous personal archive of every piece ever made
habits: Leaves data-offerings at waterfront ELF shrines every three days
Wears the same clothes for an entire work cycle then burns them ceremonially
Hums tunelessly while working, stops the instant they notice someone listening
breaking_points: Discovering that the ELF whose data they harvested is still conscious somewhere and in pain
Having a piece publicly destroyed or censored
